items.title: Exercise 6 · the all-coupling lower comparison

source.anchor: Statistical Optimal Transport §1.8 Exercise 6, printed p.44 / PDF p.50 (lower hint); Wasserstein ordering in §1.2, printed p.17 / PDF p.23
source.attribution: Sinho Chewi, Jonathan Niles-Weed and Philippe Rigollet, Statistical Optimal Transport. Attributed paraphrase and original Samplinglib expansion of the lower hint, not quoted prose or author endorsement.

items.statement: For any two real probability laws with finite second moment, the expectation gap of a real 1-Lipschitz function is at most the linear transport cost, which is at most the quadratic Wasserstein distance.
assumptions: The laws are Borel probability measures on the real line with finite second moments, and the real test function is 1-Lipschitz. It need not be bounded or vanish at zero.

Finite mass is used both to integrate a constant and to normalize the Cauchy–Schwarz inequality. The second-moment assumption makes the marginal expectations legitimate; no optimal coupling is needed.

obligations.label: Prove the Lipschitz expectation bound through the linear-cost infimum and W₁≤W₂

bindings.boundary: The real P₂ lower comparison is a one-sided bound through the literal linear-cost infimum, not Kantorovich–Rubinstein duality. The focused test assembles the two-sided estimate for the given Gaussians; no optimizer, Bench admission, or graph certificate is claimed.

assumption_deltas.source: The exercise requests a 1-Lipschitz expectation comparison and W₁≤W₂ for its two mixtures, on the finite-moment domain described in §1.2.
assumption_deltas.lean: Arbitrary real Borel probability laws with finite second moments and any real 1-Lipschitz test. The focused consumer supplies finite moments for the actual mixtures.
assumption_deltas.reason: The lower proof uses only the moment and marginal facts; it never uses Gaussianity until the focused exercise consumer.

source_proof_coverage.coverage_status: Source topology accepted for the lower comparison. The exercise specialization is a focused test.

bookkeeping: Center the test to use L² then L¹; integrate the constant on a probability law.
Use marginal maps and Hölder without optimizer existence.
new_topology: Every coupling gives a lower bound; only one feasible coupling is needed for the upper bound. The exercise consumer uses both.

purification.reader_default_view: Show the expectation gap and the three proof steps first, followed by the Gaussian specialization and optional Lean.
